edges.subject: CLN8
edges.quote: Loss-of-function mutations in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane protein CLN8 cause Batten disease, a neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorder.

edges.subject: Batten disease
edges.quote: Exogenous S,S-lysophosphatidylglycerol, but not the R,S stereoisomer, restores BMP synthesis in CLN8-deficient cells and mice and improves neurological phenotypes in cln8 mutant zebrafish.

edges.subject: CLN8
edges.quote: CLN8 acts with the lysosomal enzyme CLN5 to produce bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a signature lysosomal phospholipid with unique S,S stereochemistry.

edges.subject: CLN5
edges.quote: CLN8 acts with the lysosomal enzyme CLN5 to produce bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a signature lysosomal phospholipid with unique S,S stereochemistry.

edges.subject: CLN8
edges.quote: Here we establish that CLN8 is a glycerophosphoglycerol acyltransferase that catalyses the stereospecific acylation of S,S-glycerophosphoglycerol to generate S,S-lysophosphatidylglycerol, the CLN5 substrate in BMP synthesis.

edges.subject: Batten disease
edges.quote: Batten disease mutations impair CLN8 enzymatic activity and abolish BMP production in mice.

edges.subject: S,S-lysophosphatidylglycerol
edges.quote: Exogenous S,S-lysophosphatidylglycerol, but not the R,S stereoisomer, restores BMP synthesis in CLN8-deficient cells and mice and improves neurological phenotypes in cln8 mutant zebrafish.

edges.subject: BMP precursor supplementation
edges.quote: establish BMP precursor supplementation as a proof-of-concept therapeutic strategy.
